rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author grades the Bayhaqi narration listing Meccan surahs (al-Asr among them) as sound, all transmitters reliable scholars of Arabic.
rows.anchor: هكذا أخرجه بطوله وإسناده جيد رجاله كلهم ثقات من علماء العربية المشهورين

rows.speaker: عكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan (via Bayhaqi) list the Meccan surahs in order; al-Asr comes after al-Duha and Alam Nashrah, before al-Adiyat.
rows.anchor: عكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن قالا أنزل الله من القرآن بمكة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Bayhaqi says the ninth surah in the list is Yunus, and notes the list dropped al-Fatiha, al-Araf and Kaf-Ha-Ya-Ayn from the Meccan group.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي والتاسعة يريد بها سورة يونس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas (via Uthman b. Ata and his father, in Ibn al-Durays) gives the order of first revelations, with al-Asr after Alam Nashrah and before al-Adiyat.
rows.anchor: عثمان بن عطاء الخراساني عن أبيه عن ابن عباس قال

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Bayhaqi notes that the same first-revelation hadith has a witness in Muqatil's tafsir and in a sound mursal narration cited earlier.
rows.anchor: وللحديث شاهد في تفسير مقاتل وغيره مع المرسل الصحيح الذي تقدم

rows.speaker: أبو عياش الزرقي
rows.claim: Ahmad, via Abu Ayyash al-Zuraqi: the verse of prayer in fear (4:102) came down at Usfan between zuhr and asr.
rows.anchor: نزلت بعسفان بين الظهر والعصر كما أخرجه أحمد عن أبي عياش الزرقي

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Bazzar and others, via Hudhayfa: the verse on kalala (4:176) was revealed to the Prophet while on a journey.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة أنها نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسير له

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد
rows.claim: Bayhaqi, via Asma bint Yazid: the beginning of al-Maida was revealed at Mina; another report via Umm Amr says on a journey.
rows.anchor: أخرج البيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن أسماء بنت يزيد أنها نزلت بمنى

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd, via Muhammad b. Kab: surah al-Maida was revealed at the Farewell Pilgrimage between Mecca and Medina.
rows.anchor: نزلت سورة المائدة في حجة الوداع فيما بين مكة والمدينة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Sahih report via Umar: 5:3 was revealed on the Friday evening of Arafa during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: في الصحيح عن عمر أنها نزلت عشية عرفة يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh, via Abu Said al-Khudri: 5:3 was revealed on the day of Ghadir Khumm.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنها نزلت يوم غدير خم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author rejects both the Ghadir report and the Abu Hurayra report (18 Dhu al-Hijja on return from pilgrimage); he says neither is sound.
rows.anchor: وأخرج مثله من حديث أبي هريرة وفيه إنه اليوم الثامن عشر من ذي الحجة مرجعه من حجة الوداع وكلاهما لا يصح

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Sahih report via Aisha: the tayammum verse was revealed at al-Bayda as they were entering Medina.
rows.anchor: في الصحيح عن عائشة أنها نزلت بالبيداء وهم داخلون المدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr (Tamhid) says it is said to be at the Bani al-Mustaliq expedition; Ibn Sad and Ibn Hibban agree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر في التمهيد يقال إنه كان في غزوة بني المصطلق

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some later scholars find the Bani al-Mustaliq setting unlikely, since al-Muraysi is on the Mecca side while al-Bayda story is on the Khaybar side.
rows.anchor: واستبعد ذلك بعض المتأخرين قال لأن المريسيع من ناحية مكة

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi holds that al-Bayda lies between Medina and Khaybar, placing the tayammum revelation on the Khaybar side.
rows.anchor: وهما بين المدينة وخيبر كما جزم به النووي

rows.speaker: ابن التين
rows.claim: Ibn al-Tin is confident that al-Bayda is Dhu al-Hulayfa, which would place the tayammum revelation near Medina.
rows.anchor: لكن جزم ابن التين بأن البيداء هي ذو الحليفة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد البكري
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd al-Bakri: al-Bayda is a height in front of Dhu al-Hulayfa on the Mecca road; Dhat al-Jaysh is a day's post from Medina.
rows.anchor: البيداء هو الشرف الذي قدام ذي الحليفة من طريق مكة قال وذات الجيش من المدينة على بريد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir, via Qatada: 5:11 was revealed when the Prophet was at Batn Nakhl, when Bani Tha laba and Bani Muharib plotted against him.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن قتادة قال ذكر لنا أنها نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو ببطن نخل

rows.speaker: ابن حبيب
rows.claim: Ibn Habib says most of the Quran was revealed by day; he traced only a few examples of night revelation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن حبيب نزل أكثر القرآن نهارا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Sahihayn, via Ibn Umar: the people at Quba were at dawn prayer when news came that the Qibla verse was revealed that night.
rows.anchor: من حديث ابن عمر بينما الناس بقباء في صلاة الصبح إذا أتاهم آت

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Muslim, via Anas: the Prophet prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis when the verse on turning the face came; a man of Bani Salama announced it during dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: وروى مسلم عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي ببيت المقدس فنزلت

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Sahihayn, via al-Bara: the Prophet prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis sixteen or seventeen months; the first prayer was asr, and people turned mid-bow.
rows.anchor: في الصحيحين عن البراء أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: القاضي جلال الدين
rows.claim: Jalal al-Din (Mahalli) prefers night revelation: the Quba news reached them at dawn, and a delay from asr to subh is implausible.
rows.anchor: القاضي جلال الدين والأرجح بمقتضى الاستدلال نزولها بالليل

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar holds the stronger view is daytime revelation; news reached Bani Haritha at asr and Bani Amr b. Awf at dawn.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن حجر الأقوى أن نزولها كان نهارا

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar reads Ibn Umar's the night as a figurative use of night for part of the previous day and the next one.
rows.anchor: وقوله قد أنزل عليه الليلة مجاز من إطلاق الليلة على بعض اليوم الماضي والذي يليه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
rows.claim: Nasai, via Abu Said bin al-Mualla: the Prophet recited the turning verse on the minbar until finished, then came down and prayed zuhr.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال مررنا يوما ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاعد على المنبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author backs the daytime view with the Nasai report from Abu Said bin al-Mualla, a witness to the recitation on the minbar.
rows.anchor: قلت ويؤيد هذا ما أخرجه النسائي عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali b. Husayn: first Meccan surah is Iqra, last Meccan is al-Muminun or al-Ankabut; first Medinan is al-Mutaffifin, last is Bara ah.
rows.anchor: سمعت علي بن الحسين يقول أول سورة نزلت بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar (Sharh al-Bukhari) reports agreement that al-Baqara was the first surah revealed at Medina.
rows.anchor: وفي شرح البخاري لابن حجر اتفقوا على أن سورة البقرة أول سورة أنزلت بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author doubts the claimed consensus on al-Baqara as first Medinan surah, because of Ali b. Husayn's contrary view.
rows.anchor: وفي دعوى الاتفاق نظر لقول علي بن الحسين المذكور

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: Al-Nasafi's tafsir, citing al-Waqidi: the first surah revealed at Medina was surah al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير النسفي عن الواقدي إن أول سورة نزلت بالمدينة سورة القدر

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Abu Bakr b. al-Harith, via Jabir b. Zayd: a long Meccan order of revelation places al-Asr after al-Duha and Alam Nashrah, before al-Adiyat.
rows.anchor: حدثنا أمية الأزدي عن جابر بن زيد قال أول ما أنزل الله من القرآن بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud mushaf order (via Jarir b. Abd al-Hamid): tiwal, mi'in, mathani, mufassal; al-Asr is in the mufassal; the mushaf lacks al-Fatiha and both Mu awwidhatayn.
rows.anchor: حدثنا جرير بن عبد الحميد قال تأليف مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another scholar says one-word verses exist beyond the single case of madhamatan, e.g. al-Najm, al-Duha and al-Asr, and opening letters too.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره بل فيه غيرها مثل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Abu Amr al-Dani knows of only one word that is a verse by itself: madhamatan (55:64).
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو الداني لا أعلم كلمة هي وحدها آية إلا قوله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold the correct view that verse division is known only by revelation from the Lawgiver, as with knowing the surah.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم الصحيح أن الآية إنما تعلم بتوقيف من الشارع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari: verse division is a revealed matter with no room for analogy, which is why alif-lam-mim counts as a verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري الآيات علم توقيفي لا مجال للقياس فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author argues verse division is revealed, citing Ibn Masud's report that surahs over thirty verses were called the thirties.
rows.anchor: قلت ومما يدل على أنه توقيفي ما أخرجه أحمد في مسنده

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ahmad, via Ibn Masud: the Prophet taught him a surah of the thirties from the Ha-Mim group, which is al-Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: عن زر عن ابن مسعود قال أقرأني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سورة من الثلاثين من آل حم

rows.speaker: الموصلي
rows.claim: Al-Mawsili divides surahs into three classes by counting: no disagreement, disagreement only in detail, and disagreement in both; al-Asr falls in the detail class.
rows.anchor: قال الموصلي ثم سور القرآن على ثلاثة أقسام

rows.speaker: المدني الأخير
rows.claim: Last Medinan counter counts Watawasaw bil-haqq (103:3) as a verse and not wal-asr (103:1); the other counters do the reverse.
rows.anchor: العصر ثلاث عد المدني الأخير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One classification puts al-Asr in the group with both abrogating and abrogated verses; the no-abrogation group excludes it.
rows.anchor: والذاريات والطور والواقعة والمجادلة والمزمل والمدثر وكورت والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author doubts this classification and says it will become clear later; the no-abrogation group also names al-Asr as an exception.
rows.anchor: كذا قال وفيه نظر يعرف مما سيأتي

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki: abrogation of a recommended duty by an obligatory one, as with the initial obligation of qiyam al-layl replaced by recitation.
rows.anchor: وندب نسخ فرضا كقيام الليل نسخ بالقراءة في قوله

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki: the obligation abrogated and not to be practised by the earlier ruling; the example is abrogating confinement of adulterers by the hadd.
rows.anchor: فرض نسخ فرضا ولا يجوز العمل بالأول كنسخ الحبس للزواني بالحد

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki: obligation abrogated by obligation where the earlier ruling may still be practised, as with the verse of steadfastness (musabara).
rows.anchor: فرض نسخ فرضا ويجوز العمل بالأول كآية المصابرة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha: a verse of ten known sucklings was abrogated by five, and it was still recited until the Prophet died, showing text and ruling both abrogated.
rows.anchor: عشر رضعات معلومات فنسخن بخمس معلومات فتوفي رسول الله

rows.speaker: unnamed
rows.claim: Answer to Aisha's wording: either she meant near death, or the recitation was also abrogated but the news reached people only after the Prophet died.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد قارب الوفاة أو أن التلاوة نسخت أيضا

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashari: the verse came down and was then lifted, meaning its recitation was abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو موسى الأشعري نزلت ثم رفعت

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki: in this example both the abrogated and the abrogating verse are unrecited, and he knows no parallel.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي هذا المثال فيه المنسوخ غير متلو والناسخ أيضا غير متلو

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
rows.claim: Abrogation of ruling without recitation is very rare; many inflate the count, and Ibn al-Arabi clarified and perfected the matter.
rows.anchor: فإن المحققين منهم كالقاضي أبي بكر بن العربي بين ذلك وأتقنه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الأصبع
rows.claim: Ibn Abi al-Asbas book Al-Khawatir al-Sawanih on the secrets of surah openings is summarised here, with additions.
rows.anchor: أفردها بالتأليف ابن أبي الأصبع في كتاب سماه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الأصبع
rows.claim: Surahs open in ten kinds of speech: praise of God, letter-openers, calls, declarative sentences, oaths, and others.
rows.anchor: افتتح سور القرآن بعشرة أنواع من الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الأصبع
rows.claim: Fifteen surahs open with oaths; al-Asr is one, its oath being by the later part of the day or by the whole time.
rows.anchor: والعصر بالشطر الآخر أو بجملة الزمان

rows.speaker: unnamed
rows.claim: Fifth kind of oath-and-consequent structure: an oath followed by the consequent, as in al-Asr followed by the statement that man is in loss.
rows.anchor: والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر

rows.speaker: unnamed
rows.claim: The answer to an oath is often omitted when the sworn-by thing shows what is sworn to, e.g. Sad by the Quran implies the Quran is true.
rows.anchor: قال وأكثر ما يحذف الجواب إذا كان في نفس المقسم به دلالة على المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: unnamed
rows.claim: Oath by times such as dawn implies rites of the Hajj, which are pure worship, and honours Muhammad and Abraham.
rows.anchor: فإنها أزمان تتضمن أفعالا معظمة من المناسك وشعائر الحج

rows.speaker: unnamed
rows.claim: Oath by al-Duha and the night when still: God swears to His favour to the Prophet, which confirms his prophethood and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أقسم تعالى على إنعامه على رسوله وإكرامه له وذلك متضمن لتصديقه له

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khalawayh: no surah of three verses containing ten waws exists, except al-Asr to its end.
rows.anchor: ولا سورة ثلاث آيات فيها عشر واوات إلا والعصر إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khalawayh: no surah of 51 verses has 52 pauses, except al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: ولا سورة إحدى وخمسون آية فيها اثنان وخمسون وقفا إلا سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: الخبازي
rows.claim: Khabbazi tells Sultan Mahmud: one verse begins with ghayn for sure (40:3), and two more are disputed (30:2 and 1:7).
rows.anchor: أول ما وردت على السلطان محمود بن ملكشاه سألني عن آية أولها غين

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar's notes list four consecutive shadda-stressed passages in the Quran, quoted as phrases from 19:65, 24:40, 36:58 and 37:6.
rows.anchor: ونقلت من خط شيخ الإسلام ابن حجر في القرآن أربع شدات متوالية
